title: Block motif — eight round
subtitle: A 17 cm solid square block worked to eight rounds for large-format projects
excerpt: Eight rounds extend the solid block to 17 cm, large enough for floor cushions and throw squares worked one motif at a time rather than joined grids. The construction stays consistent — trebles packed into the sides with chain-2 corners — but the scale changes what the block can make.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 1 (1885). Large block construction standard.
heroPrompt: An eight-round solid block crochet motif in warm terracotta aran-weight cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Dense treble sides with sharp chain-2 corners, 17 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished block measures 17 × 17 cm in aran-weight cotton with a 5 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Block motif — eight round
chartDefinition.caption: Eight rounds. Chain-2 corners; solid treble sides. Side count grows by 3 per round: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24 trebles per side.

glossaryTerms.definition: A block motif worked to 8 or more rounds, producing a tile large enough to use as a standalone project element rather than joining many small tiles.

content.text: crosses the threshold from grid tile to standalone piece. Four blocks joined give a 34 × 34 cm cushion front; nine give a 51 × 51 cm small throw. Work in aran weight for this scale — the extra yarn weight gives the motif the body it needs.

Work consistently: each round adds 3 trebles per side. Keep the starting sl st and ch-3 tight on each round to prevent an uneven corner. The motif lies flat without blocking at this size; pin lightly for sharp corners if joining multiples.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 35 g of aran-weight cotton. A 5 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Work rounds 1–6 as per the six-round block. For rounds 7 and 8, sl st to corner sp, ch 3, 2 tr into corner, ch 2, 3 tr. Work tr into every side treble. 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr into each corner. Continue around. Sl st to join after each round. (Side treble counts: Rnd 7 = 18; Rnd 8 = 21.)
For a project-scale block, work the twelve-round version in chunky yarn. Or try the overlay stitch square for a different way to add pattern to a large solid motif.
